headline: Brazil’s presidential candidates push to have one another disqualified ahead of run-off
standfirst: Both candidates in Brazil's presidential election called for their rival's disqualification Tuesday over allegations of social media malfeasance, according to court filings.
body_markdown:
Both candidates in Brazil's presidential election called for their rival's disqualification Tuesday over allegations of social media malfeasance, according to court filings. Left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s campaign said they will request the annulment of right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy over alleged election interference by tech giant Meta, while Bolsonaro's team is accusing Lula of "abuse of power" in the mass sharing of government postings on WhatsApp. (France 24 Americas)

**South China Morning Post** adds: In the latest showdown from Brazil’s increasingly rancorous presidential race Tuesday, both candidates called for the disqualification of their rivals over allegations of social media malfeasance, according to court filings and campaign officials. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s campaign said they would request the disqualification of right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro on Wednesday over alleged election interference by tech giant Meta.

**The Straits Times** adds: BRASILIA, Oct 21 - Brazilian presidential candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro imposed conditions on Wednesday to disclose his bank, tax and telephone records after a challenge from President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his opponent in Sunday's election runoff.

**Al Jazeera** adds: Right-wing presidential candidate says he will release personal records if his opponent Lula meets his conditions.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by Al Jazeera, The Straits Times, South China Morning Post and France 24 Americas. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
